article.story:
AC Milan racked up their biggest win of the season under Ruben Amorim as Frosinone were beaten 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

It is now five wins in six matches for Milan, who climbed into Serie A's top four and to within five points of leaders Lazio.

It was a rampaging victory earned with room to spare, and was much needed following wins for Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus.

An own goal from Gabriele Calvani and a fourth goal of the season from Gonçalo Ramos made it 2-0 early on before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit for the visitors.

The second half quickly turned into a procession with goals from Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cissè making it 4-1 before Christian Pulisic got a goal to add some gloss to the scoreline.

Newly promoted Frosinone have been one of the surprise packages of the season, but dropped to seventh behind Juve after Luciano Spalletti's side extended their own unbeaten run to four games with a home win.

Calvani's own goal got Milan on their way, then Adrien Rabiot set up Ramos for a much-needed goal following a relatively slow start to life in Serie A.

The visitors hauled themselves back into contention midway through the first half through Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with an excellent counter-attacking play.

Substitutes Jashari and Cisse made good on Milan's dominance before Pulisic's solo run and chipped finish completed the rout to wrap up the biggest win of Amorim's time in charge.

Information from PA was used in this recap.
